newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Banks lead Hong Kong stocks to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Banks lead Hong Kong stocks to higher close.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended higher on Monday on buying in finance counters and an easing of futures-related selling pressure in the afternoon, brokers said.
"The market was dominated today by trading in just a few blue chips,"said Peter Lai, associate director at OCBC Securities.
The Hang Seng Index jumped 76.61 points to close at 13,480.75, after trading to a high of 13,503.18. Turnover was a robust HK$9.78 billion, well above Friday's HK$5.65 billion.
Turnover was fairly evenly split between selected blue chips and speculative trading in red chips, Lai said.
Covered warrants on red chips and baskets of red chips filled the most active table.
The December Hang Seng Index futures contract, which expired on Monday, closed down three points at 13,442, a discount to the market. The January contract closed off 10 points at 13,460.
International banking giant and index heavy weight HSBC Holdings gained HK$2.00 to close at HK$166.00 on turnover of HK$882.72 million, accounting for nine percent of total market turnover
Subsidiary Hang Seng Bank climbed HK$2.50 to HK95.00 on healthy turnover of HK$363.31 million.
Trading in CITIC Pacific also boosted the index. The share rose to a new high of HK$46.40, before easing to close up HK$2.00 at HK$45.60.
CITIC shares were apparently boosted by the news that management would take a 15.47 percent stake in the company, sold to them by parent company CITIC Hong Kong, brokers said.
In the property sector Henderson Land jumped HK$1.50 to HK$77.75 and New World Development gained HK$0.75 to HK$52.50.
The best performing sector of the market was Hang Seng China Enterprise Index, which put on 5.33 percent to 957.52. Guangdong Kelon led the sector with a gain of HK$0.25 to HK$4.65.
"Investors are still bullish about red chips," said Franco Pong in institutional sales at New China Hong Kong.
Pong added that despite the strong run of many of these counters, which had gained as much or more than 100 percent in 1996, many were still believed to have good upside.
China Resources climbed HK$1.50 to HK$16.85. Subsidiary Beijing Land rose HK$0.725 to HK$4.875.
The stock exchange will open for a morning session on Tuesday, will be closed on New Year's Day and resume normal trading on Thursday.
